title: Transformer-guided genetic search finds six new champion linear error-correcting codes over F₈
summary: A transformer trained to predict minimum Hamming distance, paired with a genetic algorithm and exact Brouwer–Zimmermann distance checks, found at least six previously unknown champion generalized toric codes over F₈ at dimensions 18, 22 and 38 (length 49). The article reports more than 500 champion codes in its F₈ search and up to a twofold reduction in exact distance evaluations versus random search. The six records at the three newly improved parameter settings are one paper-level coding-theory result.
ai_technology: Transformer model adapted from GPT-2, coupled with a genetic algorithm
organization: University of London; University of Warwick; University of Oxford; London Institute for Mathematical Sciences

evidence.tested: A transformer trained to predict minimum Hamming distance, paired with a genetic algorithm and exact Brouwer–Zimmermann distance checks, found at least six previously unknown champion generalized toric codes over F₈ at dimensions 18, 22 and 38 (length 49).
evidence.unknown: The codes are newly discovered mathematical constructions in the generalized toric family, with minimum distances verified computationally using established exact algorithms and compared to known records. The reported >500 total includes known/previous champion codes, while six at dimensions 18, 22 and 38 are identified as novel; these are not six separate catalog entries. The method searches a restricted family and does not establish optimal codes over all linear codes or quantum codes.
evidence.ai_role: The transformer predicts generalized toric codes’ minimum Hamming distances and guides genetic search toward promising generator matrices. Candidate champions are then checked with the Brouwer–Zimmermann algorithm and compared with known bounds; the paper reports six previously unknown champion codes at F₈ dimensions 18, 22 and 38.
